commits.message: fix(daemon): a fresh renderer's start heads the host's mailbox, and a request the close woke draws nothing (5gb)
fix(daemon): the mailbox's stats name the slot's holder and are read before their own push, and the close tests close through the mailbox (5gb)

feat(daemon): a request waits in the host for its world state, and the renderer takes one input at a time (5gb)

Every input to a renderer, events and pushes alike, passes one mailbox in the
host and is one turn, sent only once the last has answered. An input is made
as its turn comes, so what it reads of the host (a request's idle clock and
feeds, whether a click's client left, whether a session is still idle for its
close) follows every turn ahead of it. A turn's config changes land, and their
effect-done turns run, in its own place in the mailbox, so the next input
finds them landed.

A request is three steps: its config turn, a wait in the host on the session's
world state over the runs the renderer subscribes to now, then its request
turn. The wait holds no place in the mailbox, so a retire that drops a run it
waits on ends the wait on it. The collector owns the wait; the rule for what a
draw waits on moves to shared facts.

The turn never waits: the adapter's awaited calls (clicks.gone,
menuIdle.confirmClose, clickArrived, clickSettled) and the wire's call and
returned lines are deleted, and a reach crosses only as a notice. JournalTurns,
ClicksInFlight and the async in the verbs are deleted. The mailbox's holder and
queue replace journalTurns in stats, and each turn records its mailbox wait.
